analysis.is_complaint_reason: Customer expresses dissatisfaction about the app crashing and alleges material inconvenience (late rent, 40-minute branch trip) and asks for compensation (CH-1).
analysis.summary: The customer says the Harbourline app has crashed on every login attempt for about three weeks. This is her fourth call. She could not pay her rent on time and had to travel to a branch 40 minutes away. She wants the app fixed and compensation. Earlier contacts only gave reinstall and clear-cache advice. It is not confirmed whether an IT ticket was raised. She uses an Android phone; the app version is unknown. No evidence is on file.

timeline.event: First contact: app login crash, advised to reinstall.
Still crashing, advised to clear cache.
Still crashing after reinstall. IT ticket possibly raised, unconfirmed.
Fourth call, logged as complaint. Android phone, app version unknown.
Customer could not pay rent on time and went to a branch 40 minutes away.

analysis.severity_reason: Repeated service failure: four contacts about the same issue (CH-6 Medium). Loss is not quantified and no other High trigger is shown. Late rent consequences are unknown.

vulnerability.suggested_support: No indicators recorded. Ask sensitively about support needs, since the late rent may hint at financial pressure, and about any rent late fees.

analysis.routing_reason: A persistent app login crash over three weeks needs technical investigation, so ESC-1 points to Digital Operations. No fraud, lending or vulnerability referral trigger is evident.
